Note::TexAccessor::render¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::TexAccessor::render(std::int64_t max_passes = 1) const

Build A Readable Unicode Projection¶

render() converts common authored TeX notation into compact readable Unicode text. It expands simple local macros, unwraps common text commands, renders fractions and roots, maps recognized symbols, converts supported scripts to Unicode superscripts or subscripts, removes math delimiters, and collapses layout whitespace. It is useful for previews, search labels, logs, and compact display where retaining the TeX source is not required.

This is deliberately not a TeX compiler. It does not execute packages, load files, lay out boxes, evaluate conditionals, apply fonts, or preserve a round trip to the source. Unknown control words are discarded while balanced brace contents remain readable. A TeX linebreak becomes whitespace. Escaped symbols are unescaped near the end of the projection. Use to_text() for a prose-oriented extraction that removes mathematics, or keep the original Note when exact source fidelity matters.

max_passes controls recursive expansion of simple zero-argument macros found in each cell. The default 1 performs one substitution pass. Larger values permit chains such as \A -> \B -> text to resolve; processing stops early when a pass makes no change. The value must be positive and is validated before the receiver is read. It is a work bound, not an output style.

The operation is out-of-place and shape preserving. Its output is Text even when all visible content disappears. Undefined state propagates after argument validation; defined non-Text input rejects. Work is approximately linear in the input for each macro pass, followed by linear lexical transformations; large max_passes values should therefore be reserved for genuinely recursive macro chains.

Example 1: Mathematics And Readable Symbols¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"($\frac{1}{2}\alpha + x^{2} - y_1$)",
    R"(\textbf{Rate} \leq \infty; \unknown{kept})",
    R"(escaped \\alpha and \$5)"});
std::cout << source.tex().render() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["(1)/(2)α + x² - y₁", "Rate ≤ ∞; kept", "escaped alpha and $5"]

The unknown wrapper disappears but its braced text remains. The doubled backslash is treated as a TeX linebreak, so the following alpha is ordinary text rather than the Greek control word.

Example 2: Matrix Shape Is Preserved¶

const auto grid = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{R"($x_1$)", R"(\alpha)", "plain", ""},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << grid.tex().render() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["x₁", "α"],
  ["plain", ""]
]

Example 3: Recursive Macro Expansion¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note(
    R"(\newcommand{\A}{\B}\newcommand{\B}{done}\A)");
std::cout << "one=" << source.tex().render(1).scalar()
          << " two=" << source.tex().render(2).scalar() << '\n';

Output¶

one= two=done

After one pass, \A has become unresolved \B; the readable projection drops that unknown control word. Two passes reach the visible body done.

Example 4: Invalid Work Bounds Reject First¶

try {
  (void)pluss::Note::undefined().tex().render(0);
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "render(0): rejected\n";
}

Output¶

render(0): rejected

Example 5: Undefined State And Dtype¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha << "undefined="
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().render().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1}).tex().render();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "render Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

undefined=false
render Int64: rejected
